summary: Intermittent high TTFB and 504s caused by proxy write stalls when request-metadata headers grow during streaming
description: Issue summary: Over the last 24 hours Nimbus Analytics is seeing intermittent elevated Time-To-First-Byte (TTFB) spikes and occasional 504 Gateway Timeouts on long streaming completions. Impact: customer-facing endpoints for large chat sessions experience degraded latency and occasional request failures, affecting multiple product customers using the same dedicated tenant. Environment: prod (us-east-1), dedicated capacity, requests traverse the external edge gateway (Envoy-based) -> internal ingress -> serving-runtime. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a long-running chat completion with multi-turn context and tracing baggage headers enabled. 2) Stream responses back to client for ~60-120s. 3) Observe intermittent periods where bytes stop flowing for ~30-90s and then connection resets with 504 or timeout. Observed behavior: interleaved TTFB spikes, streaming stalls with zero bytes for tens of seconds, followed by 504s. Logs/metrics: edge-proxy write buffer growth correlates with increasing per-request header sizes (baggage/trace metadata), envoy stats show upstream_bytes_buffered and downstream_write_failed. Expected behavior: steady streaming without stalls, within latency SLOs. Additional notes: problem appears bursty and correlated with sessions that rotate trace/authorization metadata frequently (client library re-attaches baggage headers every turn).
comments: 2026-03-12 10:23 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reported bursts of 504s and long TTFB during streaming calls. Captured sample request ids and initial trace headers. Asked for reproduction details and asked customer to reduce sampling rate of tracing as a short test.

2026-03-12 11:05 UTC - SRE (Marco): Found elevated envoy downstream_write_buffered_bytes on the edge fleet serving the tenant. Noted several streams hitting large header frames on HTTP/2 endpoints. Opening investigation into HPACK/HTTP2 compression interaction and proxy buffering settings.
2026-03-12 13:02 UTC - Customer (Nimbus): Confirmed they enabled per-turn baggage and rotated an auth token every 30s. They can reproduce reliably when baggage payload goes >8KB combined headers.

2026-03-12 15:40 UTC - SRE (Marco): Rolled temporary routing rule to route the tenant to a gateway pool with extended idle timeout and disabled header coalescing for streaming routes. Observing immediate reduction in 504s for the tenant; collecting metrics for 12h window.

2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and recommended the following: reduce per-turn baggage size, avoid rotating large auth cookies on every turn, and upgrade client SDK to v2.3.1 which includes streaming header streaming optimization.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: header growth is forcing HTTP/2 HPACK to emit large header frames that interact poorly with our edge proxy write buffer and downstream connection windowing, causing transient backpressure and write stalls.
Confirmed correlation between requests where cumulative request headers >6KB and occurrences of downstream_write_blocked metric on envoy (edge) and sudden increase in upstream write retries.

Observed edge proxy configured with 60s idle_send_timeout and aggressive proxy_buffering enabled for HTTP/1 routes; for HTTP/2 routes header compression and buffer accounting differs and large HPACK dynamic tables can inflate frame sizes.

Reproduced locally by streaming a 90s session while incrementally appending 1KB baggage headers per turn: observed write stalls at the edge after header frame growth and subsequent 504s from internal ingress when write stall exceeded idle_send_timeout.

Telemetry: linked dashboard panels - Edge Envoy write/backpressure, gateway 504 counts, tenant token rotation histogram (collected), and per-connection header size distribution. Relevant traces: trace-ids captured in ticket comments.
Temporary mitigation applied: route tenant to expanded-timeout gateway pool and disabled proxy buffering for streaming endpoints; immediate drop in 504 rate from ~4.3% -> 0.6% in sample window.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-12 15:40 UTC): tenant routed to gateway pool with idle_send_timeout extended to 180s and proxy_buffering disabled for /v1/streaming endpoints. Customer confirmed improvement.
Short-term customer action: reduce per-turn baggage headers and avoid rotating large auth cookies per-turn. Rollout note: communicated SDK patch v2.3.1 to Nimbus to minimize header churn.

Planned fixes: engineering to 1) add per-route header-size rejection early (413) with clear error to guide clients, 2) add streaming path which bypasses buffer coalescing and uses windows-aware writes for HTTP/2, 3) increase observability for per-connection header growth and backpressure alerts. Assigned INT-4512 to implement gateway-level hard limits and improved metrics.

Post-incident follow-up: draft runbook update and confluence page created (see related_confluence_pages). Recommend scheduled change to deploy streaming-path improvements in canary by 2026-03-20 then full rollout.
